description.narrative:
''Public Private Development Partnership for Renewable Energy Skills Training and Women Economic Empowerment in Somalia" är ett program som sträcker sig över fyra år 2018-2022, inklusive en 6-månaders startfas. Programmet kommer att inrikta sig på två övergripande mål 1) Förbättrade tekniska kunskaper för att driva solenergi i Somalia och på så sätt öka marknaden samt tillgången till energi till fattiga och 2) Ökad andel kvinnor med stärkt ekonomiskt egenmakt i Somalia. För att uppnå dessa mål har ILO föreslagit att följande specifika aktiviteter (delmål) genomförs a) förbättra förvaltningen samt samordningen inom energisektorn, b) bidra till kompetensutveckling inom sektorn för förnybar energi för att öka tillgängligheten och svara mot nuvarande och framtida marknadsbehov c) förbättra arbetsmöjligheter inom energisektorn d) förbättra kvinnors roll inom energisektorn och särkskilt förnybar energi. e) öka efterfrågan på förnybara energiprodukter, och f) förbättra den långsiktiga kapaciteten och hållbarheten hos civila samhällsorganisationen i Somalia.
Den föreslagna insatsen kommer att genomföras i samarbete med somaliska företag, civila samhällsorganisationer, den svenska handelskammaren, den amerikanska handelskammaren, arbets- och socialdepartementet, energidepartementet, utbildningsdepartementet samt handelsdepartementet i Somalia. Programmet kommer att föregås av en sex månaders startperiod för att kunna färdigställa förberedande aktiviteter som kommer att underlätta implementeringen av insatsen.
Sida har en total budget på SEK 49,6 miljoner. Ungefär SEK 12,2 miljoner av budgeten kommer att överföras till ILO:s samarbetspartners för att genomföra en del av projektverksamheten. Den totala programbudgeten kommer att utvecklas under startfasen där bidrag från berörda samarbetsaktörer kommer att inkluderas både i form av medel och som egen insats.

The International Labour Organisation (ILO) has applied to Sida for funding of 49.6 million SEK to carry out the ‘Public Private Development Partnership for Renewable Energy Skills Training and Women’s Economic Empowerment in Somalia during the period 2018-2022.
The intervention will aim at two goals 1) Improved technical skills to drive solar technology deployment in Somalia in order to grow the market and raise energy access to the poor and 2) Increased proportion of economically empowered women in Somalia. To achieve the above mentioned goals, ILO has proposed to specifically; a) improve management and coordination within the power sector; b) contribute to skills development for the renewable energy sector that is available and responds to current and future market needs; c) improve integration of Somalis in the energy sector workforce; d) enhance the role of women in emerging renewable energy market; e) increase demand for renewable energy products; f) improve the long-term capacity and sustainability of Somali Civil Society Organizations and g) Strengthen the ability of women to advocate for policy and regulatory reforms.
The proposed intervention will be implemented in partnership with select Somali private companies, civil society organizations, Chamber of Trade Sweden, Chamber of Commerce and, the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs as well as the Ministry of Education. The programme will be preceded by a six month inception phase.
The intervention has a total budget of 49.6 MSEK which will be wholly funded by Sweden. Approximately 12.2 MSEK of the budget will be forwarded to partners to implemented part of the project activities.

This training programme takes a multi-faceted approach with the overall objective of increasing technical skills in the electricity and renewable energy sector in Somalia and consequently enabling deployment of renewable energy throughout the country. The intervention also aims to economically empower women in Somalia.

The program entered into its final year of implementation and it continues to work and contribute to key government priorities. The National Development Plan (NDP-9) 2020-2024 identifies womens economic empowerment and skills development in several sectors including the renewable energy sector as a catalyst for growth.
With regards to the Renewable Energy (RE) component, the curriculum was developed, discussed with FGS and private sector and adopted. The selected ToTs completed their virtual training and also physical training at Strathmore University in Nairobi. In total there were 11 Trainer of Trainers (10 male and 1 female) all completed practical training and all 11 graduated in November 2021.
The group started with i) Power generation practical exercises at Strathmore Energy Research Centre. ii) Eastlands College of Technology for building services exercises then concluded with iii) Power transmission and distribution practical training at the Institute of Energy Studies and Research (IESR-KPLC).
With regards to equipment delivery and installation, most of the equipment was delivered to Banadir Training Institute (BTI) run by BECO and NECSOM training center in 2021 following shipping disruptions caused by Covid 19 and delays in issuing cargo clearance at Mogadishu port. However, some equipment's yet to be received by the training centers. BTI is the only training Centre that administered entry exams, a total of 90 students passed and enrolled for various courses and have received. All trainees were placed on job practical skills training three days per week to gain hands-on work experience. Despite the progress made during this reporting period, there were challenges and lessons learned which some have been mitigated in the process of adopting the alternative working and training modalities.
In the Women's Economic Empowerment (WEE) component, the program supported zamzam foundation and Simad University to improve their service to better serve women entrepreneurs. This was done through a gender self-assessment known as WE-Check. A report was published on the outcome of the WE-Check self-assessment process which listed a number of recommendations including; develop quality leadership by including women in decision-making and train/mentor women leaders, improve and implement organizational policies to highlight gender-sensitive strategies in programming and ensure staff are training, and to increase fundraising and resource mobilization to support gender equality and women entrepreneurship. SIMAD University completed the process in late 2021 and with the action plan, hope to begin implementing improvements in 2022. With regard to ensuring women have access to relevant training programs, the project in 2021 saw 338 entrepreneurs in Mogadishu and Garowe receive training in either how to improve their business or how to improve their exhibition skills. To help increase market opportunities for women entrepreneurs, the project sought to make available a platform where women entrepreneurs would be able to showcase their business, come in contact with existing or new clients, identify other women entrepreneurs and make sales. The platform was launched in 2021 online (due to COVID restrictions) and is now housed with the Somali Chamber of Commerce and Industries as a means to ensure its upkeep and sustainability. The platform is called Goobaal, https://www.goobaal.so/aboutus
The program was affected by Covid-19, internal financial challenges, extended period without a project manager, project staff off work on sick leave, difficulties in completing payments on time due to staff absences and challenges in communication between project staff and finance colleagues in Nairobi and Addis Ababa. Visa challenges affected 7 ToTs that couldn't travel to Nairobi to complete their advanced training.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
